newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Thursday on a lack of market-moving news, traders said.
The most actively traded July 1997 contract rose 50 yuan to 3,260 yuan ($393) per tonne. It opened at 3,280 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,380 and a low of 3,235 yuan per tonne.
September fell 38 to 3,298, November dropped 11 to 3,320, the January 1998 contract rose 31 to 3,320 and March gained 60 to 3,275 per tonne.

Combined volume rose to 17,800 tonnes from 12,300 tonnes. "Most investors stayed on the sidelines today on a lack of market-moving news," one trader said. "With prices moving in a narrow range for a few days, major institutions were reluctant to build new positions."
Traders said they expected soybean prices to move narrowly in slow trading in the next few days.
